**My reasoning as this farmer:**

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. I have about 10 mu of flat irrigated field. I finished primary school but I've been farming since I was a boy — I know this land better than any book.

Here in Quzhou we do wheat and maize. That's what everyone does, that's what the land is suited for, that's what the grain stations buy. I'm not going to experiment with something fancy. My wheat goes in around October and comes off in June, then I turn around and plant maize on the same ground. By October I harvest maize, then back to wheat. This rotation has worked my whole life.

I'll plant the improved wheat variety the seed shop in town has been selling the last few years — my neighbor Old Liu used it and got good yields. For maize I'll use hybrid seed, that郑单958 type, same as always. The hybrids yield better than open-pollinated, everyone knows this.

For fertilizer I'll put down compound fertilizer before planting wheat, then top-dress with urea at jointing. For maize I'll do the same — base fertilizer plus a top-dress. I put maybe a little more nitrogen than the extension posters say because my yields drop if I cut back — I learned that the hard way years ago.

I'll irrigate wheat four times: the seedling water, the winter water before it freezes, jointing water, and grain-fill water. The groundwater here is still accessible. Maize needs less since it rains in summer, but I'll do one supplemental irrigation if July is dry.

I'll spray pesticides on wheat twice — once for aphids around heading, once for disease. Maize once for corn borer.
